title: Nuclei without atoms
hook: Explore the evidence behind a cosmic question.

knows: Light and gravity help astronomers study the universe.
doesNotKnow: Light nuclei formed while the universe was still extremely hot. Later cooling made it possible for electrons to remain bound to nuclei as neutral atoms.

misconception: A learner may choose: Electrons did not exist until galaxies formed
objective: Use the visual model to reason about: Why did stable neutral atoms form later than the first light nuclei?

claims.text: Question, correct answer and explanation: Why did stable neutral atoms form later than the first light nuclei? The universe had to cool enough for electrons to remain bound. Light nuclei formed while the universe was still extremely hot. Later cooling made it possible for electrons to remain bound to nuclei as neutral atoms.
Visual caption: Cooling allows neutral atoms. The SVG is a conceptual illustration, not measured data or a scale model.

recall.question: Why did stable neutral atoms form later than the first light nuclei?
options: The universe had to cool enough for electrons to remain bound

Nuclei and neutral atoms always formed simultaneously
